questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Add a correct question tag: You are travelling to Gulu tomorrow, ____?
questions.a: aren't you?

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Add a correct question tag: She didn't attend the concert, ____?
questions.a: did she?

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Add a correct question tag: Let us begin the journey, ____?
questions.a: shall we?

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Change to reported speech: "I am going to visit my aunt," said Maria.
questions.a: Maria said that she was going to visit her aunt.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Change to reported speech: "We shall board the bus at six o'clock," the children said.
questions.a: The children said that they would board the bus at six o'clock.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Change to direct speech: He said that he had enjoyed the trip.
questions.a: "I enjoyed the trip," he said. (Also acceptable: "I have enjoyed the trip," he said.)

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete with the correct form: If I ____ (know) about the party, I would have come.
questions.a: had known

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: If she had revised well, she ____ (pass) the examination.
questions.a: would have passed

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the adjective formed from each: care, beauty, friend, excite.
questions.a: care → careful (or careless); beauty → beautiful; friend → friendly; excite → exciting (or excited).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in: The journey was very ____ (tire) and we were all ____ (tire) when we arrived.
questions.a: The journey was very tiring and we were all tired.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Change to the active voice: The compound was swept by the pupils.
questions.a: The pupils swept the compound.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite using "going to": I intend to visit my grandparents next holiday.
questions.a: I am going to visit my grandparents next holiday.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: a friend you write letters to but may never have met.
questions.a: A pen pal.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: extra lessons given to help a learner who is behind.
questions.a: Remedial classes.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Use the word commence in a sentence of your own.
questions.a: Learner's sentence, for example: The lessons will commence at eight o'clock.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite beginning with the words given: He finished his chores and then went to play. — Having …
questions.a: Having finished his chores, he went to play.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the meaning of up-country and use it in a sentence.
questions.a: Up-country means away from the city, in the villages. Example: My father travelled up-country to see his parents.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write four sentences describing your plans for the next holiday, using "going to" in each.
questions.a: Learner's answer. Each sentence must use "am/is/are going to" + verb, for example: I am going to help my mother in the garden.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short paragraph (about six sentences) about the most interesting thing you did last holiday. Use the past tense.
questions.a: Learner's paragraph. It should be in the past tense, in one paragraph, with a topic sentence, correct punctuation and capital letters.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give two differences between direct speech and reported speech.
questions.a: In direct speech the exact words are used and put in quotation marks, while in reported speech the words are not exact and there are no quotation marks; in reported speech the tense moves one step back and words such as today, here, this change to that day, there, that.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the difference between a formal and an informal letter.
questions.a: An informal letter is written to a person you know well, such as a friend or relative, using friendly language; a formal letter is written to somebody in their official position, using polite official language, and it includes the receiver's address and a heading (Re:).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name any six parts of a formal letter in the order in which they are written.
questions.a: Sender's address; date; receiver's address; salutation; heading (Re:); body; complimentary close; signature and full name. (Any six in order.)

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name any five parts of an informal letter.
questions.a: Sender's address; date; salutation; introduction; body; conclusion; complimentary close; first name. (Any five.)

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Which complimentary close is used when a letter begins with Dear Sir?
questions.a: Yours faithfully.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Which complimentary close is used when a letter begins with Dear Mrs Achieng?
questions.a: Yours sincerely.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the full meaning of: Re:, c.c., pp, N.B., P.S.
questions.a: Re: — reference; c.c. — carbon copy; pp — on behalf of; N.B. — note well; P.S. — a note added at the end of a letter.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the meaning of maiden name and vacancy.
questions.a: Maiden name — a woman's family name before she married. Vacancy — a job or place that is free and needs to be filled.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Where is the receiver's address written, and in which type of letter?
questions.a: On the left-hand side, below the date, and only in a formal letter.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Form adverbs from: careful, happy, true, good, fast.
questions.a: careful → carefully; happy → happily; true → truly; good → well; fast → fast.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in with the correct word: There is ____ anyone who replied to my letter. (hardly / hard)
questions.a: hardly

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite beginning with the word given: Only 30% of the people applied. — Barely …
questions.a: Barely 30% of the people applied.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Use is likely to in a sentence of your own.
questions.a: Learner's sentence, for example: He is likely to come tomorrow.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write the present continuous form: I ____ (write) to invite you to my party.
questions.a: am writing

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any four rules to follow when filling in an official form.
questions.a: Any four of: write in capital letters; use black or blue ink; write the surname first where asked; write dates as day/month/year; leave nothing blank — write N/A; do not overwrite; sign where a signature is required.
accepted: write the surname first where asked
sign where a signature is required

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: You are Nakato Sarah of P.O. Box 12, Masaka. Write the address and date part of a letter you would write on 4th May 2026.
questions.a: For example: P.O. Box 12 Masaka 4th May 2026 (written at the top right, with no name above the address)

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write the heading (Re:) you would use in a letter applying for the post of a cook.
questions.a: RE: APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF A COOK (written and underlined).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short formal letter (about eight lines) to your head teacher requesting permission to be away from school for two days.
questions.a: Learner's letter. It must have: the sender's address and date (right), the head teacher's address (left), Dear Sir/Madam,, an underlined RE: line, a polite body giving the reason and dates, Yours faithfully, a signature and the full name in capitals.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short informal letter (about eight lines) to your friend telling him or her about your new school.
questions.a: Learner's letter. It must have: the sender's address and date (right), Dear …, a friendly opening, a body in paragraphs, a closing greeting, Yours affectionately/Your friend, and the first name only. No receiver's address and no Re: line.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give two reasons why people write informal letters and two reasons why they write formal letters.
questions.a: Informal: to greet or give news, to invite a friend, to thank somebody, to apologise (any two). Formal: to apply for a job or a place, to ask permission, to complain, to request information (any two).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Correct the mistake: Dear Sir, … Your's Sincerely, Ann.
questions.a: It should read: Dear Sir, … Yours faithfully, Ann. — the close must match Dear Sir, Yours has no apostrophe, and faithfully takes a small letter.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: a person sitting an examination.
questions.a: A candidate.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: the person who watches over candidates in the examination room.
questions.a: An invigilator.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the meaning of aggregate and malpractice.
questions.a: Aggregate — the total of the grades scored in the subjects. Malpractice — cheating or any dishonest act in an examination.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is leakage in an examination, and give one of its effects?
questions.a: Leakage is examination questions getting out before the examination. One effect: the examination may be cancelled and the candidates disqualified (it also makes the results unfair and spoils the name of the school).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: You must revise your work ____ ____ you will fail. (two words)
questions.a: or else

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: We look forward to ____ (write) our examinations in November.
questions.a: writing

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite using Despite: Although she was sick, she came for the examination.
questions.a: Despite being sick, she came for the examination. (Also: Despite her sickness, she came for the examination.)

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite using In spite of: Although it rained heavily, the paper started on time.
questions.a: In spite of the heavy rain, the paper started on time.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Join using Whereas: Many candidates passed. Okello failed.
questions.a: Whereas many candidates passed, Okello failed.
accepted: Whereas many candidates passed, Okello failed.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: Cheating ____ lead to the closure of an examination centre. (could / can hardly)
questions.a: could

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in: The paper was ____ difficult, so many candidates complained. (quite / rather)
questions.a: rather

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in with the correct possessive: This pen is ____ (I) and that one is ____ (they).
questions.a: This pen is mine and that one is theirs.
accepted: This pen is mine and that one is theirs.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in: The school lost ____ trophy because ____ raining heavily. (its / it's)
questions.a: The school lost its trophy because it's raining heavily.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any five rules a candidate must follow in the examination room.
questions.a: Any five of: arrive early; carry your examination card and instruments; leave books, notes and phones outside; listen to the invigilator; write your name and index number on every sheet; read all instructions first; use ink; work silently and alone; never copy or exchange work; check your work before handing in.
accepted: carry your examination card and instruments
write your name and index number on every sheet
check your work before handing in

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any five ways of preparing well for an examination.
questions.a: Any five of: make and follow a revision timetable; revise a little every day; do past papers under time; ask the teacher what you do not understand; join a serious discussion group; keep your card and instruments safely; eat well and get enough sleep.
accepted: make and follow a revision timetable
ask the teacher what you do not understand
keep your card and instruments safely
eat well and get enough sleep

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Say exactly what each instruction asks you to do: underline, tick, arrange, state, explain.
questions.a: Underline — draw a line under the word; tick — put a ✓ against the right answer; arrange — put the items in the correct order; state — give a short answer without explaining; explain — give a fuller answer in sentences.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What three things should a candidate check on the examination card?
questions.a: His or her names, the index number, and the examination centre (and the subjects entered).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give two effects of examination malpractice on a candidate.
questions.a: The candidate's results are cancelled (disqualification), and he or she may be barred from sitting the examination for some years; it also brings shame to the candidate, the family and the school.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Use the word invigilator in a sentence of your own.
questions.a: Learner's sentence, for example: The invigilator told us to stop writing when the time was over.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short paragraph (about six sentences) advising a P.6 pupil on how to prepare for examinations.
questions.a: Learner's paragraph. It should be one paragraph, in the present or future tense, with clear advice such as making a revision timetable, revising daily, doing past papers, asking teachers, resting well and avoiding cheating.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is electronic media? Give any four examples.
questions.a: Electronic media are means of communication that use electricity or electronic devices. Examples: radio, television, the internet, DVD and CD players (any four).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the meaning of: presenter, studio, aerial, eject.
questions.a: Presenter — the person who introduces and runs a programme; studio — the room from which programmes are made or broadcast; aerial — the rod or wire that receives the signal; eject — to push out, for example a disc from a player.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the full meaning of CD, DVD and CD-ROM.
questions.a: CD — compact disc; DVD — digital versatile disc; CD-ROM — compact disc read-only memory.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: If you ____ (tune) in at seven o'clock, you will hear the news.
questions.a: tune

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: If I ____ (have) a radio, I would listen to the farming programme.
questions.a: had

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: If I were you, I ____ (not buy) that old player.
questions.a: would not buy

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: Sarah is a good presenter and so ____ Doreen.
questions.a: is

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: Musa does not like adverts and ____ does Peter.
questions.a: neither

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite using needn't have: You switched off the television, but it was not necessary.
questions.a: You needn't have switched off the television.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Change to reported speech: "I am watching the news," said Father.
questions.a: Father said that he was watching the news.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Change to reported speech: "Connect the extension cable," the teacher told us.
questions.a: The teacher told us to connect the extension cable.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any four kinds of programmes broadcast on radio or television.
questions.a: Any four of: news, sports, music, drama, documentaries, talk shows, farming programmes, children's programmes, religious programmes, adverts.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What five questions must a good news item answer?
questions.a: Who, what, when, where, why (and how).
accepted: Who, what, when, where, why (and how).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short announcement (about three sentences) telling P.7 pupils about a briefing on Monday.
questions.a: Learner's answer, for example: All P.7 pupils are informed that a briefing about the examinations will take place on Monday at 9:00 a.m. in the school hall. Every candidate must attend with a pen and a notebook. For more information, see the head teacher.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short advert (about three sentences) for a shop selling school bags.
questions.a: Learner's answer, for example: Are you looking for a strong school bag? Visit Mukwano Bag Shop, opposite the market, for strong bags from only 25,000 shillings. Hurry while stocks last!

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any four advantages and four disadvantages of electronic media.
questions.a: Advantages: fast information; learning and research; entertainment; communication over long distances (any four). Disadvantages: high cost of gadgets and data; bad content and time wasting; eye strain and little exercise; fraud; false news (any four).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any five ways of caring for electronic gadgets.
questions.a: Any five of: keep them dry and dust-free; hold discs by the edges; eject discs before switching off; keep away from strong sunlight and heat; switch off and unplug during storms; use the right cables and voltage; do not overload a socket; keep away from small children.
accepted: keep away from strong sunlight and heat
switch off and unplug during storms
use the right cables and voltage

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Use I don't like and I like each in a sentence about programmes.
questions.a: Learner's sentences, for example: I like watching the weather forecast. / I don't like long adverts.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the difference between If 1 and If 2, with one example of each.
questions.a: If 1 is about something real and likely and uses If + present simple, will + verb: If it rains, we shall stay indoors. If 2 is about something imagined or unlikely now and uses If + past simple, would + verb: If I had a television, I would watch the news.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short dialogue (six lines) between two friends discussing their favourite programmes.
questions.a: Learner's dialogue. It should have two speakers named, a new line for each speaker, correct punctuation and natural language, for example: Ann: Which programme do you like most? Ben: I like the sports news. And you?

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the difference between a right and a responsibility, with one example of each.
questions.a: A right is something a child is entitled to, for example the right to education; a responsibility is a duty the child is expected to perform, for example attending school regularly and doing homework.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name any five rights of a child and the responsibility that goes with each.
questions.a: Any five pairs from the table, for example: the right to food — helping with the chores; the right to education — attending school regularly; the right to medical care — keeping clean and reporting illness; the right to play — playing safely; the right to protection — reporting abuse.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the meaning of: child labour, dropout, early marriage, bad touches.
questions.a: Child labour — making a child do heavy or harmful work; dropout — a learner who leaves school before finishing; early marriage — marrying while still a child; bad touches — touching a child's private parts or in a way that is not right.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What should a child do if somebody tries to touch him or her wrongly?
questions.a: The child should say NO loudly, get away from the person, and tell a trusted adult at once — a parent, teacher, religious leader, police officer or child helpline. The child must not keep it a secret, and it is never the child's fault.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: All children ____ ____ go to school. (two words)
questions.a: ought to

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: You should move in groups ____ ____ ____ avoid child abuse. (three words)
questions.a: in order to

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: You ____ provide food to your children ____ you risk going to prison.
questions.a: You either provide food to your children or you risk going to prison.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in the correct relative pronoun: The teacher ____ helped the orphan was rewarded.
questions.a: who

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in the correct relative pronoun: The goat ____ leg was broken has been treated.
questions.a: whose

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in the correct relative pronoun: This is the sanctuary ____ the animals are kept.
questions.a: where

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite in the future continuous: We shall discuss children's rights this time tomorrow.
questions.a: This time tomorrow, we shall be discussing children's rights.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite using the past perfect: The poacher escaped. Then the rangers arrived.
questions.a: The poacher had escaped before the rangers arrived.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name the five freedoms of animals.
questions.a: Freedom from hunger and thirst; freedom from discomfort; freedom from pain, injury and disease; freedom to express natural behaviour; freedom from fear and distress.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any five ways in which people abuse animals.
questions.a: Any five of: overloading and overworking; beating and stoning; tying legs tightly or hanging animals on bicycles; starving them or giving dirty water; keeping them in dirty, tight places; not treating sickness; poaching; burning bush; abandoning pets.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any five ways of caring for animals.
questions.a: Any five of: give clean water and enough feed; build a clean dry shelter; treat and vaccinate them; handle them gently; give them space; protect them from thieves and wild animals; report cruelty and poaching.
accepted: give clean water and enough feed
protect them from thieves and wild animals

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the full meaning of: UWA, UWEC, WSPA, USPA, WCU.
questions.a: UWA — Uganda Wildlife Authority; UWEC — Uganda Wildlife Education Centre; WSPA — World Society for the Protection of Animals; USPA — Uganda Society for the Protection of Animals; WCU — Wildlife Clubs of Uganda.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Form nouns from these verbs: protect, behave, decide, educate, capture.
questions.a: protect → protection; behave → behaviour; decide → decision; educate → education; capture → captivity (or capture).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite using Much as: Although a cow is an animal, it also needs protection.
questions.a: Much as a cow is an animal, it also needs protection.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite using need not have: Obbo tied his goat on the motorcycle carrier, but it was not necessary.
questions.a: Obbo need not have tied his goat on the motorcycle carrier.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short paragraph (about six sentences) explaining why children should protect animals.
questions.a: Learner's paragraph. It should be one paragraph with clear reasons, such as: animals also feel pain; they give us food, work and money; wild animals bring tourists and income; caring for animals shows kindness; the law protects them; and animals cannot speak for themselves.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the meaning of: pollution, erosion, habitat, conservation.
questions.a: Pollution — making air, water or land dirty and harmful; erosion — the wearing away and carrying off of soil; habitat — the natural home of a plant or animal; conservation — the protection of nature and its resources.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the difference between flora and fauna.
questions.a: Flora means all the plants of an area, while fauna means all the animals of an area.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the two meanings of the word refuse and use each in a sentence.
questions.a: As a noun it means rubbish: The refuse was collected on Monday. As a verb it means to say no: They refuse to pay the fine.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name any six activities that damage the environment.
questions.a: Any six of: cutting down trees, bush burning, overgrazing, poor farming on slopes, draining swamps, dumping garbage, smoke from factories and vehicles, mining and quarrying, poaching, pouring waste into rivers.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any five reasons why the environment should be protected.
questions.a: Any five of: to keep reliable rainfall; to protect the soil; to keep air and water clean; to protect the habitats of plants and animals; to keep supplying raw materials, food and medicine; to prevent floods, drought and disease; to attract tourists; to leave enough for future generations.
accepted: to keep air and water clean
to protect the habitats of plants and animals
to leave enough for future generations

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name any six ways of protecting the environment.
questions.a: Any six of: afforestation and reafforestation; terracing and contour ploughing; mulching and cover crops; crop rotation and manure; controlled grazing; proper waste disposal; protecting wetlands and river banks; using solar and biogas; making and obeying laws; educating people.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: We must protect our environment ____ have rain.
questions.a: to

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: Our well was polluted, ____ we did not have clean water.
questions.a: so

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite beginning with Since: We shall have no rain because the forests have been cut.
questions.a: Since the forests have been cut, we shall have no rain.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: If we don't build terraces, the soil ____ (erode).
questions.a: will erode

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: If we ____ (not cut) the trees, we would have had more rain.
questions.a: had not cut

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: Bush burning ____ ____ ____ overgrazing cause degradation. (three words)
questions.a: as well as

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: The head teacher as well as the pupils ____ (be) planting trees yesterday.
questions.a: was

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Form abstract nouns from: beautiful, poor, strong, protect, conserve, free.
questions.a: beautiful → beauty; poor → poverty; strong → strength; protect → protection; conserve → conservation; free → freedom.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite using had to: It was necessary for us to build terraces to protect our soil.
questions.a: We had to build terraces in order to protect our soil.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any four ways of disposing of waste properly.
questions.a: Any four of: using dustbins and waste baskets; digging a rubbish pit; composting food waste; burning dangerous waste in an incinerator; recycling plastic, paper and metal; taking waste to a proper dumping site.
accepted: burning dangerous waste in an incinerator
taking waste to a proper dumping site

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short message of not more than fifteen words for a poster about tree planting.
questions.a: Learner's message, for example: "Plant a tree today — save the rain for tomorrow."

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short paragraph (about six sentences) about the importance of protecting the environment.
questions.a: Learner's paragraph. It should have a topic sentence, three or four supporting reasons in the present tense, correct punctuation and a closing sentence.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the difference between If 1 and If 3, with one example of each.
questions.a: If 1 is about something real and likely: If we plant trees, we will get more rain. If 3 is about something in the past that did not happen: If we had planted trees, we would have had more rain.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Use each of these words in a sentence of your own: mulching, incinerator, degrade.
questions.a: Learner's sentences, for example: Mulching keeps the soil moist during the dry season. / The hospital burns its waste in an incinerator. / Bush burning can degrade the land.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name the three types of marriage mentioned in the syllabus.
questions.a: Cultural (customary) marriage, religious marriage and state (civil) marriage.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the meaning of: introduction (kwanjula), bride price, best man, matron of honour.
questions.a: Introduction (kwanjula) — the ceremony where the man is formally introduced to the girl's family; bride price — property or money given in a customary marriage; best man — the man who supports the bridegroom; matron of honour — the married woman who supports the bride.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: the bunch of flowers carried by a bride.
questions.a: A bouquet.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Arrange these wedding events in the correct order: reception, engagement, wedding service, introduction.
questions.a: Engagement → introduction → wedding service → reception.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: a woman whose husband has died.
questions.a: A widow.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: a person chosen to take the place of the dead person.
questions.a: An heir (a female one is an heiress).
accepted: An heir (a female one is an heiress).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the meaning of: condolences, mourner, shroud, cremate.
questions.a: Condolences — words expressing sorrow to the bereaved; mourner — a person who attends a funeral to show sorrow; shroud — the cloth in which a body is wrapped; cremate — to burn a dead body to ashes.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in: Neither the bride nor the bridegroom ____ (be) late.
questions.a: was

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in: Both the maid of honour and the best man ____ (be) present.
questions.a: were

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite using prefer: He likes a religious marriage more than a state one.
questions.a: He prefers a religious marriage to a state one. (Also: He prefers having a religious marriage to having a state one.)

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in the correct relative pronoun: The church ____ they wedded is near the market.
questions.a: where

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in the correct relative pronoun: The woman ____ was the bride is my aunt.
questions.a: who

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in the correct emphatic pronoun: The President ____ attended the state funeral.
questions.a: himself

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in: ____ mourners arrived early, so the service started late. (Few / A few)
questions.a: Few

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite in the past perfect: The mourners left. Then the rain started.
questions.a: The mourners had left before the rain started.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite in the future perfect: They will complete the funeral rites by Sunday.
questions.a: By Sunday, they will have completed the funeral rites.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Rewrite beginning Despite the fact that: Although Abdul was a rich man, he was buried in two shrouds.
questions.a: Despite the fact that Abdul was a rich man, he was buried in two shrouds.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Form adjectives from: culture, religion, tradition, ceremony.
questions.a: culture → cultural; religion → religious; tradition → traditional; ceremony → ceremonial.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short dialogue (six lines) between two people planning to attend a wedding.
questions.a: Learner's dialogue. It should name two speakers, start a new line for each speaker, and use correct punctuation and natural language.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short paragraph (about six sentences) describing a ceremony you have attended.
questions.a: Learner's paragraph. It should be one paragraph in the past tense, saying what the ceremony was, where and when it took place, what happened in order, and how the writer felt.
